newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Pearson buys into S.African papers.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Pearson buys into S.African papers.

text.p: Media group Pearson, publisher of Britain's Financial Times newspaper, on Monday said it had bought a stake in two South African business publications as part of its strategy to gain a foothold in key financial newspaper markets.
Pearson agreed to buy a 50 percent holding in Business Day and Financial Mail for 11.5 million pounds ($18.89 million) as it sees both publications benefit from its expertise in financial publishing.
The acquisition also includes the television production company African Business Channel.

"We see great opportunities in South Africa...both in print and electronically as well," Pearson executive director David Bell said. "What we do is bring in our expertise in producing a good financial newsparer."

Business Day currently has daily sales of 40,200, while the weekly Financial Mail sells 31,000 copies. Both publications will establish strong ties with the Financial Times, which will lend its international experience, Pearson said.
Bell stressed the purchase would not bring about changes in the style and coverage of the South African papers.
"We do not dictate -- and nor seek to dictate the political and the editorial view. That is entirely a matter of the editor," Bell said.
The acquisition comes hot on the heels of Pearson's mega purchase last month of U.S. publisher Putnam Berkley for $336 million.
The South African deal, however, is relatively small and analysts said it gave no pointers to any change in strategy by American Marjorie Scardino, who will take over as chief executive in January.
"It is a cautious expansion into potentially developing territory," said Anthony de Larrinaga of broker Panmure Gordon.
In view of the political changes in South Africa, Pearson said it opted for a joint venture with a local partner rather than taking full control over Business Day and Financial Mail.
"Because of the way the country is changing it would be wise to have a joint venture," Bell said.
Pearson continued to look at potential investments in the European business press, such as in the Netherlands where it is in talks to buy the privately-owned Financieele Dagblad, he said.
"We are going to review the situation this week," Bell said after editorial staff at the Dutch paper last week voted on a potential acquistion by Pearson.
"We understand they were not enthusiastic about us, or indeed anybody."
Pearson also owns the French business newspaper Les Echos, which Bell said was doing very well in terms of sales, but suffering from the sluggish French economy.
"We are very pleased with the performance of Les Echos...in what is a very difficult market," he said, while margins at the Financial Times were improving.
"Our trading margins are moving up nicely. By some measurements our margins have done better than at the Wall Street Journal, which is really the benchmark we've set," he said.
